statements.statement: Owner: Executive director, until the board names an owner
statements.label: default
statements.reason: The call named no policy owner, so the template default applies.

statements.statement: Next review: In 12 months
statements.label: default
statements.reason: The call gave no review date, so the 12-month default applies.

statements.statement: We want AI to give providers their evenings back. We must protect patient information and keep people in charge of care.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Matches the providers' hope and leadership's breach worry.

statements.statement: All staff, volunteers, contractors and board members.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: The call is silent on scope, so the template's general default applies.

statements.statement: AI scribe from our health record vendor: three pilot providers only, covered by BAA, may hold patient visit information.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Call confirms a signed BAA and a three-provider pilot.

statements.statement: New tools: Nadia approves anything touching patient information, after a BAA. Beth approves the rest.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Matches Beth's description of who approves new tools.

statements.statement: Accounts: Use your work email, not a personal account. Turn off vendor training on what you type.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default for accounts; the call is silent.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Everyone, now: Any AI tool, signed in with work email, for work with no information about a real person.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call settled nothing here, so the template default applies.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Look up general clinical questions with no patient information.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dr. Okafor described clinicians doing this with no patient data.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Draft patient education handouts for clinician review.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Handouts with ChatGPT were described, and Jordan said a clinician should review them.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Draft letters like appointment reminders and sliding fee letters, with no names.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Jordan described these letters, hoping they are written without names.

statements.section: What you can use AI for
statements.statement: Pilot providers only: AI scribe drafts visit notes.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Matches the three-provider pilot and the scribe tool line.

statements.statement: New use of patient information in an approved tool — Nadia
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Nadia approves anything that could touch PHI, per Beth.

statements.statement: New clinical use — Dr. Okafor, medical director
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Beth said clinical uses also need Dr. Okafor.

statements.statement: AI billing or coding help — Your manager
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call called billing risky but named no approver, so the manager default applies.

statements.statement: AI translation of patient materials — Your manager
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Call raised translation as risky but named no approver, so the manager default applies.

statements.statement: Information that never goes into an AI tool: diagnoses, medications, behavioral health notes, substance use records, HIV status, reproductive health, immigration status, income documents, insurance numbers, staff files, donor list, passwords.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Each type was named by Beth; passwords are the standing default.

statements.statement: HIPAA covers patient records; substance use records carry extra federal protection.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Beth said both.

statements.statement: Nobody uses AI to make clinical decisions.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dr. Okafor said a clinician decides and signs.

statements.statement: Nobody uses AI to decide sliding fee eligibility.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Beth said a person decides from the documents.

statements.statement: Read every word of a scribe note before signing. AI once added a medication we decided against.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dr. Okafor said this and gave the example.

statements.statement: Check AI work for facts, names, numbers and tone. The sender is responsible.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Template default review line.

statements.statement: A clinician reviews AI handouts. Check AI billing codes.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Jordan said clinicians review handouts; Beth flagged coding errors as a compliance risk.

statements.statement: AI may help look something up or draft a note. A person decides.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Matches Dr. Okafor on lookup and scribe drafting, with the person deciding.

statements.statement: Tell patients when the scribe is listening. They can say no.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dr. Okafor described the verbal consent script in the pilot.

statements.statement: Reviewed handouts need no AI label. Chatbots must say they are not people.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Jordan said both.

statements.statement: Tell Nadia right away if patient information may have gone into an AI tool.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Dr. Okafor said problems go to Nadia.

statements.statement: Nadia runs the HIPAA breach process. Reporting mistakes is not punished.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Nadia runs the breach clock per the call; the no-punishment line is the template default.

statements.statement: The executive director owns this until the board names someone.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: Matches the owner default.

statements.statement: Managers go over it with new staff.
statements.label: default
statements.reason: The call is silent on how staff learn the policy; generic default.

statements.statement: The compliance committee reviews changes; the board approves them.
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Beth said the committee reviews and the board approves the policy.

statements.statement: Do we roll the scribe out to all providers after the pilot, in about three months?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Beth raised this as unsettled.

statements.statement: Should behavioral health providers use the scribe at all?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Beth said those providers are split.

statements.statement: Do we approve tools staff use now, like ChatGPT, OpenEvidence and UpToDate AI search?
statements.label: contradicts
statements.reason: Settled elsewhere: 'Everyone, now' allows any AI tool and allowed uses rely on those tools; the call said the scribe is the only approved AI, so either drop this question or make it only about paying for or approving them.

statements.statement: What do we tell funders like HRSA and the state about our AI use?
statements.label: supported
statements.reason: Beth said funders haven't asked yet but will; the call settled no answer.

missed: Written Spanish materials sometimes go through Google Translate; the policy only asks for manager approval and does not say it is currently unapproved or that certified interpreters are used for visits.
The scribe use needs the verbal consent script, which is not named in the policy.
Donors who are also patients make the donor list extra sensitive.
Jordan said staff are unsure what is allowed and some use AI secretly; the policy does not say how to ask questions or that staff will not be punished for past use.
Whether translation or billing approvals might need Nadia or Dr. Okafor instead of a manager was not addressed.

missed: Patient information may not go into ChatGPT or other consumer tools, and the policy never says so; it would help to say so near the Everyone, now line.
The policy doesn't say who may use OpenEvidence and UpToDate AI search, which are unofficial clinical tools.
Written Spanish materials are sometimes run through Google Translate; the policy only requires approval and doesn't mention certified interpreters or review by a qualified translator.
Staff are unsure what is allowed and some use AI secretly; the policy lacks a line inviting staff to ask questions.
A phone bot or chatbot replacing front desk staff was a worry; the policy doesn't state a position.
